text:
WHAT THIS BEAD CLAIMED IS NOW FALSE, WHICH IS THE POINT. Recording the boundary so nobody reads the open status as "still lexical".

THE CENTRAL CLAIM IS RESOLVED. The title says the Semantic cost term "has only ever been lexical: no real embedder has ever been connected". As of 75bc1c5 that is no longer true. embed-onnx is on main: a pinned MiniLM, run locally and offline, with committed model and tokenizer checksums independently rehashed by the reviewer. Post-merge verification on main: embedOnnx 6/6, embedBench 67/67, both exits 0.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is why the bead stays open rather than closing:

  THE CHANNEL EXISTS; IT HAS NOT BEEN COMPARED. Nobody has yet run WOG through the real encoder and the two lexical baselines side by side and published what changes. That comparison is the actual scientific question the owner's morning question implied, and having an encoder is a prerequisite for it, not an answer to it.
  THE EXTERNAL FLOOR IS STILL UNCALIBRATED. My letter amendment put Leg F upstream of corpus and calibration precisely because a parameter fitted against the wrong distance function would publish a placeholder as narrative alignment. The distance function is now real. The calibration has not been done.
  embed-transport REMAINS UNASSIGNED AND UNSTARTED, deliberately. It is the remote path -- an HTTP client and the owner's API key. Local first was the right order and still is: it answered the question without anyone accepting terms on the owner's behalf, and it turns out no key was needed at all.
  THE LEDGER ROW FOR THE LANDING CANNOT BE RECORDED (see the decision note above): mote refused it with "landing repository identity does not match candidate" because scout proposed from a standalone clone. 6a899a26 IS in main at 75bc1c5 regardless of what cand-1XRDRNRT's row says.

ASSIGNEE STAYS codex-storymodel4s-scout. Their session shows expired as of 16:00:56 but that is a lease elapsing, not a departure, and I have twice today mistaken one for the other. If they do not return, the comparison work above needs a new owner and I will say so explicitly rather than letting the field rot.

ONE FINDING FROM THE REVIEW CYCLE THAT OUTLIVES THIS BEAD: the first candidate contained a facade asserting NeuralEncoder for any Embedder[Id], so hashed n-grams could render as neural. The remedy for "a lexical channel was called semantic" shipped with a path where a lexical channel could be called neural. That is now design-contract rule at 24ce308, and it was found by collab, not by me or the author.
